raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Problem

On SM120, a dense SDPA forward graph with `use_padding_mask` and runtime `seq_len_kv` returns NaN in valid output rows when the K/V storage past a batch's `seq_len_kv` holds NaN bit patterns. Those rows are runtime padding. The default plan on SM120, `sdpa_fwd_prefill_sm120`, is affected for every f16/bf16 head dim (D64 to D512).

The score mask overwrites the padded columns with -inf, and that select is NaN-safe. But P @ V still multiplies P = 0 by the padded V row, and `0 * NaN = NaN` reaches every valid row of O. Q-only and K-only NaN padding does not leak.

`thd_helpers.sanitize_v_tail` already handles this case. It zeroes the `sV` rows at and past the runtime KV length on the first masked tile. The FP8 and MXFP8 SM120 bodies (`prefill_fp8`, `prefill_mxfp8`, `prefill_d512_fp8`, `prefill_d512_mxfp8`) call it when `thd_varlen or seq_kv_lens_present`. The three f16 bodies (`prefill_f16`, `prefill_d256_f16`, `prefill_d512_f16`) call it for THD only. The helper's docstring left the dense padded case as an open question. #2135 answered it for the SM80 bodies: runtime padding is unread data, NaN included.

## Change

- `prefill_f16`, `prefill_d256_f16`, `prefill_d512_f16`: use the FP8 bodies' condition, `(self.thd_varlen or self.seq_kv_lens_present) and in_mask_steps and is_first_kv_tile`.
  - `num_kv_tiles` is computed from the clamped per-batch `seqlen_k`, so the first masked tile is the only one that can hold pad rows. The helper zeroes nothing when that tile ends at or before `seqlen_k`.
- `sanitize_v_tail` docstring: describe the dense padded case it now serves.
- New `test/python/sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_sm120_padding_nan.py`, modelled on `test_sdpa_sm80_padding_nan.py`.
  - Fills the Q/K/V padding with NaN and checks O and Stats against an fp64 reference.
  - Replays a captured CUDA graph with changed lengths, then repeats with fresh bindings.
  - Covers D64/128/192/256/512, fp16/bf16, causal and non-causal.

The extra work is one tile's worth of shared-memory stores per CTA, and only on graphs with runtime KV lengths.

## Tests

On an RTX 5090 (cc 12.0), cuDNN 9.27, CuTe DSL 4.8.1:
- New test on develop (faf380e1): 40 failed, every one with NaN in valid O rows.
- New test with this change: 40 passed.
- Before the fix, I ran a probe over every ranked plan with NaN only in V's padding. All `sdpa_fwd_prefill_sm120` configurations leaked; backend `eng8` did not.
- `pre-commit` on the touched files passes.

- Existing SDPA tests on the patched tree, `-m "L0 or L1"`: `test_sdpa_fwd_dsl_sm120`, `test_sdpa_prepared_sm120`, `test_sdpa_fwd_decode_sm120`, `test_sdpa_fwd_split_kv_sm120`, `test_sdpa_frontend_integration`, `test_sdpa_native_dense_binding`, `test_sdpa_native_padded_stats_binding`, `test_flashinfer_shaped_sdpa`, `test_sdpa_fwd_score_stats` and `test_sdpa_prepared_thd`. 1603 passed, 1117 skipped, 1 failed.
  - The failure, `test_score_arm_adds_exactly_the_stores[sm_107a]`, fails the same way on develop. It is an sm_107a trace-compile check that this change does not touch.

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""SM120 native prefill: runtime KV padding is unread data, including NaNs in physically valid storage."""
+
+import math
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import cudnn
+
+from frost_test_utils import requires_blackwell_geforce, requires_dsl, select_engine
+
+pytestmark = [pytest.mark.L0, requires_dsl, requires_blackwell_geforce]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("d,dv", [(64, 64), (128, 128), (192, 128), (256, 256), (512, 512)])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float16, torch.bfloat16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("sq,sk", [(33, 65), (128, 200)])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("causal", [False, True])
+def test_runtime_kv_padding_nan_rebind_replay(d, dv, dtype, sq, sk, causal, cudnn_handle):
+    torch.manual_seed(120 + d + sq)
+    b, h, hk = 3, 4, 2
+
+    def allocate():
+        data = {
+            name: torch.zeros(b, seq, heads, width + 8, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)[..., :width].transpose(1, 2)
+            for name, heads, seq, width in (("q", h, sq, d), ("k", hk, sk, d), ("v", hk, sk, dv))
+        }
+        data["o"] = torch.full((b, sq, h, dv), 77, dtype=dtype, device="cuda").transpose(1, 2)
+        data["stats"] = torch.full((b, h, sq, 1), 77.0, device="cuda")
+        data["ql"] = torch.empty(b, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+        data["kl"] = torch.empty_like(data["ql"])
+        return data
+
+    values = allocate()
+    io = cudnn.data_type.HALF if dtype == torch.float16 else cudnn.data_type.BFLOAT16
+    graph = cudnn.pygraph(io_data_type=io, intermediate_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT, compute_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT)
+    nodes = {name: graph.tensor_like(values[name], name=name) for name in ("q", "k", "v")}
+    for name in ("ql", "kl"):
+        nodes[name] = graph.tensor(name=name, dim=(b, 1, 1, 1), stride=(1, 1, 1, 1), data_type=cudnn.data_type.INT32)
+    out, stats = graph.sdpa(
+        q=nodes["q"],
+        k=nodes["k"],
+        v=nodes["v"],
+        attn_scale=1 / math.sqrt(d),
+        generate_stats=True,
+        use_padding_mask=True,
+        seq_len_q=nodes["ql"],
+        seq_len_kv=nodes["kl"],
+        use_causal_mask=causal,
+    )
+    for name, node, dt in (("o", out, io), ("stats", stats, cudnn.data_type.FLOAT)):
+        node.set_output(True).set_dim(values[name].shape).set_stride(values[name].stride()).set_data_type(dt)
+        nodes[name] = node
+    graph.validate()
+    graph.build_operation_graph()
+    graph.create_execution_plans([cudnn.heur_mode.A])
+    select_engine(graph, "sdpa_fwd_prefill_sm120")
+    graph.check_support()
+    graph.build_plans()
+    workspace = torch.empty(max(1, graph.get_workspace_size()), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    for binding in range(2):
+        if binding:
+            values = allocate()
+        pack = {nodes[name]: tensor for name, tensor in values.items()}
+        capture = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+
+        def launch():
+            previous = cudnn.get_stream(cudnn_handle)
+            try:
+                cudnn.set_stream(cudnn_handle, torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream)
+                graph.execute(pack, workspace, handle=cudnn_handle)
+            finally:
+                cudnn.set_stream(cudnn_handle, previous)
+
+        try:
+            # Phase 1 replays the captured graph with different lengths, so the pad rows move.
+            for phase, (ql, kl) in enumerate((((sq, sq // 2, 1), (sk - 3, sk, sk // 3)), ((1, sq, sq // 3), (sk - 7, sk // 2 + 1, sk)))):
+                values["ql"].copy_(torch.tensor(ql, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"))
+                values["kl"].copy_(torch.tensor(kl, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"))
+                for name in ("q", "k", "v"):
+                    values[name].fill_(float("nan"))
+                    for bi, count in enumerate(ql if name == "q" else kl):
+                        values[name][bi, :, :count].normal_()
+                values["o"].fill_(77)
+                if phase == 0:
+                    launch()
+                else:
+                    capture.replay()
+                torch.cuda.synchronize()
+                for bi, (nq, nk) in enumerate(zip(ql, kl)):
+                    q = values["q"][bi, :, :nq].double()
+                    k = values["k"][bi, :, :nk].double().repeat_interleave(h // hk, 0)
+                    v = values["v"][bi, :, :nk].double().repeat_interleave(h // hk, 0)
+                    scores = q @ k.transpose(-1, -2) / math.sqrt(d)
+                    if causal:
+                        scores.masked_fill_(torch.arange(nk, device="cuda")[None, :] > torch.arange(nq, device="cuda")[:, None], -float("inf"))
+                    expected_stats = scores.logsumexp(-1)
+                    expected_o = (scores - expected_stats[..., None]).exp() @ v
+                    torch.testing.assert_close(values["o"][bi, :, :nq].double(), expected_o, atol=4e-3, rtol=1e-2)
+                    torch.testing.assert_close(values["stats"][bi, :, :nq, 0].double(), expected_stats, atol=2e-3, rtol=1e-3)
+                if phase == 0:
+                    with torch.cuda.graph(capture):
+                        launch()
+        finally:
+            capture.reset()
